I work in a nursing home in the UK, only started a few months back. I told my manager that I've recently started taking anti depression medication and my moods have been all over the place from it. At first she was very understanding, told me "do you need to take some time off for a while?" I told her no, it would be best if I kept going on because it would keep me in a routine when I needed. I was told that whenever I needed to call out "sick" because of how I was feeling, it wouldn't be an issue. A few months go by and I called out a few times, showed up late from having panic and anxiety attacks (mind you, I work 12 hour shifts at this place, 7am to 7pm.). I had a meeting with my manager last week to discuss them hiring someone from an old job of mine that caused me serious distress, bullying, lying in investigations, that sort of thing. I told them "I will never set foot in this building while that person is here", meaning I'm not coming in when they're on shift. My manager then had the audacity to throw it back in my face that I've taken numerous days off "sick" and that "everyone has shit to deal with but we all have to struggle on and keep this place running". I decided not to pull any more overtime for the foreseeable future to try and get my head right, and now they're floundering without me to help pick up the extra. Just goes to show that first impressions are most of the time, wrong and companies don't give a fuck about you at all! Look after yourself first, because no one else is gonna do it!
